priority.when: At the start to understand project structure
priority.why: Get overview of files that may have changed

priority.when: To check git status and run tests
priority.why: Essential for understanding changes and verifying functionality

priority.when: To examine modified files in detail
priority.why: Get full context of changes for thorough review

priority.when: To find related files and patterns
priority.why: Identify all files that may be affected by changes

tool.name: execute_command - git_status
tool.purpose: Check what files have been modified
tool.when_to_use: At the beginning of review process
tool.expected_output: On branch main Changes not staged for commit: M src/userService.ts M tests/userService.test.ts

usage_notes.note: Use this to identify which files need review
Look for both modified (M) and new (??) files
Pay attention to untracked files that should be reviewed

tool.name: execute_command - git_diff
tool.purpose: View the actual changes made to files

parameter.name: cached
parameter.description: Use cached diff for faster review

usage_notes.note: Use this to understand exact changes made
Review both additions (+) and deletions (-)
Pay attention to context lines (@@)

tool.name: execute_command - git_log
tool.when_to_use: When reviewing related changes or understanding context
tool.expected_output: abc1234 fix(auth): handle null response in user endpoint def5678 refactor(api): extract session management 9012ef feat(user): add login and registration endpoints

usage_notes.note: Helps understand recent changes to the codebase
Useful for identifying related work

tool.name: execute_command - npm_test
tool.expected_output:
PASS src/userService.test.ts getUser ✓ should return user when found ✓ should throw error when not found 12/12 passed (100%)
Test Suites: 1 passed, 1 total Tests: 12 passed, 12 total Snapshots: 0 total Time: 2.456 s

usage_notes.note: All tests must pass before code can be committed
Check test coverage percentage if available
Look for any skipped or failing tests

tool.name: execute_command - npm_lint
tool.purpose: Run linting tools to check code quality
tool.when_to_use: During code review for additional quality checks
tool.expected_output:
src/userService.ts 15:3 error 'user' is defined but never used no-unused-vars 23:7 warning Missing semicolon semi
✖ 2 problems (1 error, 1 warning)

usage_notes.note: Linting catches style and potential issues
Use as supplemental to manual review, not replacement
Fix linting errors before final approval
Only stage files that have been reviewed and approved
Verify files being staged match the review scope

tool.name: execute_command - git_commit
tool.purpose: Create commit with conventional commit message
tool.expected_output:
[main 8f3a2b1] feat(auth): add user login functionality
1 file changed, 45 insertions(+) create mode 100644 src/auth/login.ts

usage_notes.note: Follow conventional commits format strictly
Include type, scope, subject, body, and footer
Reference related issues in footer

tool.name: execute_command - git_push
tool.expected_output: To github.com:username/repo.git * [new branch] abc1234..def5678 -> main (forced update)

usage_notes.note: Verify push completed successfully
Note the commit hash for reference

tool.name: read_file
tool.purpose: Read file contents for detailed review
tool.when_to_use: When examining specific files identified by git status

parameter.name: files
parameter.description: Array of file paths to read

usage_notes.note: Read both the modified file and related test files
Read configuration files that may be affected
Read documentation for context

tool.name: search_files
tool.purpose: Find files matching patterns across project
tool.when_to_use: When looking for related files or patterns

usage_notes.note: Use to find all test files for a feature
Search for configuration files related to changes
Find all files that import a changed module
